sum: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals reported on November 8 that a single subcutaneous dose of investigational CIDEBsiRNA produced sustained liver-fat reductions in adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. The company said the findings were presented at AASLD The Liver Meeting 2026 and published simultaneously in The New England Journal of Medicine. The details come from a Regeneron Pharmaceuticals release.

In the Phase 1/2 study, 30 participants received one of four CIDEBsiRNA dose levels and 10 received placebo. At week 36, liver fat reductions among treated participants ranged from 58% to 80%, compared with a mean 2.9% reduction for placebo, measured by MRI-PDFF. Liver fat fell below 5% in 62% of treated participants and in none of the placebo group.

Mean alanine aminotransferase levels declined across all dose groups, while aspartate aminotransferase changes moved in the same direction. The company said the primary goal was to assess safety and tolerability, with liver fat and liver-injury markers serving as secondary endpoints.

Overall adverse-event rates were generally similar between the CIDEBsiRNA and placebo groups. All events were mild or moderate except for one severe, serious hyperglycemia event in a treated participant; Regeneron said it was not caused by the study drug and was later attributed to adult-onset Type 1 diabetes. No participants discontinued treatment, and no nausea or vomiting events were reported in the CIDEBsiRNA groups.

The candidate remains investigational. Recruiting Phase 2a, Phase 2b and Phase 3 studies will test whether the early MRI-based improvements translate into durable effects on liver injury, disease progression and tissue-level outcomes.

sum: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals said on Sunday, November 8, that a single investigational CIDEB siRNA dose produced sustained liver-fat reductions in adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. The company released the results ahead of a virtual investor event on Tuesday, November 10, focused on its cardiometabolic and MASH pipeline.

According to Regeneron's release, the Phase 1/2 first-in-human trial tested one subcutaneous dose across four dose levels in 30 participants receiving CIDEB siRNA and compared them with 10 placebo recipients. Safety and tolerability were the primary objectives, while liver fat and liver-injury markers were secondary measures.

Liver fat fell by 58% to 80% at week 36 among CIDEB siRNA recipients, measured by MRI-PDFF. The reductions had reached 49% to 72% at week six. The placebo group recorded a mean reduction of 2.9% at week 36.

At week 36, liver fat was below 5% in 62% of treated participants, compared with none in the placebo group. Regeneron also said 93% of treated participants achieved at least a 30% reduction in liver fat, a threshold associated with histological MASH resolution. Improvements in ALT and directionally similar changes in AST were sustained through week 36.

The findings remain early clinical evidence rather than approval data. Regeneron said longer-term safety and histologic outcomes are being evaluated in ongoing Phase 2a, Phase 2b and Phase 3 studies. The company stated that the potential uses of CIDEB siRNA are investigational and have not been evaluated by a regulatory authority.

Regeneron scheduled a virtual Regeneron Roundtable for Tuesday, November 10, at 8:30 a.m. Eastern time to discuss its cardiometabolic and MASH programs. The company said a replay would be archived on its website for at least 30 days.

sum: Regeneron stock traded at 798.20 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 15:00 CET on Friday, November 6, 2026. The company is drawing investor attention after strong third-quarter growth and an expanded antibody alliance with Sanofi.

In its October 30 financial release, Regeneron said third-quarter 2026 revenue rose 36 percent from the year-earlier period to 5.116 billion US dollars. GAAP net income increased 33 percent to 1.949 billion US dollars, while diluted GAAP earnings per share rose 35 percent to 18.45 US dollars.

Management expects to recognize the upfront payment as collaboration revenue in the fourth quarter.

Chief Executive Leonard Schleifer said the company has a pipeline of about 50 product candidates and highlighted continued progress in immunology, oncology, metabolic disease and rare disease. The company expects an FDA decision on cemdisiran for generalized myasthenia gravis in November 2026. items.t: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ:REGN) Stock Rockets 25% As Investors Are Less Pessimistic Than Expected
sum: The Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ:REGN) share price has done very well over the last month, posting an excellent gain of 25%. The bad news is that even after the stocks recovery in the last 30 days, shareholders are still underwater by about 2.6% over the last year.

In spite of the firm bounce in price, you could still be forgiven for feeling indifferent about Regeneron Pharmaceuticals' P/E ratio of 16.3x, since the median price-to-earnings (or "P/E") ratio in the United States is also close to 18x. However, investors might be overlooking a clear opportunity or potential setback if there is no rational basis for the P/E.

Regeneron Pharmaceuticals could be doing better as it's been growing earnings less than most other companies lately. One possibility is that the P/E is moderate because investors think this lacklustre earnings performance will turn around. You'd really hope so, otherwise you're paying a relatively elevated price for a company with this sort of growth profile.
The only time you'd be comfortable seeing a P/E like Regeneron Pharmaceuticals' is when the company's growth is tracking the market closely.

If we review the last year of earnings, the company posted a result that saw barely any deviation from a year ago. Whilst it's an improvement, it wasn't enough to get the company out of the hole it was in, with earnings down 11% overall from three years ago. Therefore, it's fair to say the earnings growth recently has been undesirable for the company.

Turning to the outlook, the next three years should generate growth of 3.9% per annum as estimated by the analysts watching the company. That's shaping up to be materially lower than the 11% per annum growth forecast for the broader market.

In light of this, it's curious that Regeneron Pharmaceuticals' P/E sits in line with the majority of other companies. It seems most investors are ignoring the fairly limited growth expectations and are willing to pay up for exposure to the stock. These shareholders may be setting themselves up for future disappointment if the P/E falls to levels more in line with the growth outlook.
